note: A `defmodule`/`defprotocol` whose name is not an `alias` node (`defmodule name do` names a module after a VARIABLE; `defmodule Module.concat(A, B) do` after a computed expression) has no name to own anything. `declarationName` already refused to invent one (P3), but the scope stack then kept the ENCLOSING module, so every declaration inside was attributed to it. Measured before the fix: 10 declarations in 5 corpus files and the wrong edges it published — `contains ExceptionTest -> foo`, `exports ExceptionTest -> foo`, `contains MapTest -> name/age/hello/world`, `contains ModuleTest -> hello`. The rule now pushes an UNNAMED scope: the member symbols are still published (a declaration is a declaration) but carry no owner, so `contains` and `exports` cannot name one. A `defstruct` inside an un-nameable module is NOT published either, because a struct's name IS its module's name. Falsifiers: mutants elixir/unnamed-module-scope-dropped, elixir/unnamed-module-scope-leaked, elixir/unnamed-module-struct-kept.
